topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecturer, sets out the course context, and outlines the core learning objectives concerning cancer causation.

topics.label: Cancer biology and intrinsic mutational processes
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define cancer as an evolutionary genetic disease shaped by cellular microenvironments, endogenous metabolic damage, and inherited genetic susceptibilities.

topics.label: Environmental exposures, epidemiology, and the bad-luck debate
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the relative contributions of environmental factors versus random mutational events using public health examples and global epidemiological trends.

topics.label: Infectious agents and Burkitt lymphoma
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how oncogenic pathogens contribute to cancer development, focusing on the epidemiological and molecular mechanisms of Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Mechanisms of chemical, dietary, and physical mutagens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how specific environmental and dietary compounds cause DNA damage through direct interaction or metabolic activation.

topics.label: Tumor promotion, inflammation, and host susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore non-mutagenic mechanisms of carcinogenesis, including chronic inflammation, tumor promoter signalling, and developmental windows of tissue vulnerability.

topics.label: Methodologies for identifying and testing carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics review the genomic, epidemiological, animal, and in vitro approaches used to determine the carcinogenic potential of environmental agents.
